title: (Updated) Microsoft Outlook: New event duplication capability
summary: Microsoft Outlook is adding a "Duplicate event" feature, allowing users to quickly create new events based on existing ones without re-entering details. The rollout began in late September 2026 and will complete by early December 2026. No action or compliance changes are required.
body:
Updated November 6, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We are adding the ability to duplicate an event in Microsoft Outlook. From the event details, users can select Duplicate event to quickly create a new event based on an existing event without re-entering the same details.

[Rollout schedule]

- General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High): Rollout began in late September 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026 (previously late October).[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

- Users who create events in Microsoft OutlookPlatforms and services

- Microsoft OutlookWhat will happen

- A new Duplicate event option will appear in Microsoft Outlook event details.- Users can quickly create a new event based on an existing event without re-entering the same details.[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

Updated November 6, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We are adding the ability to duplicate an event in Microsoft Outlook. From the event details, users can select Duplicate event to quickly create a new event based on an existing event without re-entering the same details.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High): Rollout began in late September 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026 (previously late October).

  • Users who create events in Microsoft Outlook

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Outlook

What will happen
